subject: Post-call: FintechCo logging & PII redaction follow-ups
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: FintechCo logging & PII redaction follow-ups

Hi Alex — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and the items we said we'd follow up on from our discovery call:  

1) Scope and ask (what you confirmed):
- You want to capture request/response logs for troubleshooting and monitoring but need automated redaction of PII (names, account numbers, SSNs, payment tokens) from any persisted logs.
- Retention policy: 90 days for full logs, with the option to keep redacted traces and telemetry up to 12 months for analytics.
- Data residency: primary production in us-west, long-term archived telemetry must remain in the US.

2) Specific questions we committed to answer by Tuesday:
- Can Redwood redact sensitive fields automatically at ingress (request / response) and in headers/trace IDs?
- What controls are available to prevent sensitive headers (e.g., Authorization, Cookie) from being stored?
- How does redaction interact with our KV cache and prefix caching? Any risk of leaking PII via cache keys?
- Where are logs stored, and can we point them to your VPC/private bucket for storage?

Next steps (proposed):
- I will attach our redaction controls doc and a SOC2-mapping spreadsheet for your security team to glance at.
- Dylan will scope an optional follow-up call with your security engineer to go deeper on the header/trace-id questions.
- If this looks good, we can draft a mutual action plan and attach it to the HubSpot deal.

Answers in short: yes for automated redaction at ingress (configurable), yes for header scrubbing, and we have cache-safe keying options — details below in the follow-up email.

Open items for you: please confirm which exact headers you need preserved (if any) and whether your retention window needs to be shorter than 90 days.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redaction_controls_v1.pdf (see section 2.1 for field patterns), soc2_mapping.xlsx

Subject: Re: Post-call: FintechCo logging & PII redaction follow-ups

Thanks Marissa — clear recap, much appreciated. A few clarifications from our side:  

- We need Authorization and a custom header X-Customer-ID redacted from any persisted logs, but X-Trace-ID should be preserved for tracing back to our systems (we will hash it on our side if needed). Can Redwood preserve trace IDs but ensure they cannot be used to reconstruct PII?
- Cache concern: we use a prefix-based key that includes an account id in the key. We need to confirm that any persisted cache keys are redacted or masked in logs.
- Data residency: yes, all stored logs and any exported telemetry must remain in the US; cross-region replication is not acceptable.

Also tagging our security engineer (security@fintechco.com) — they'll want the SOC2 mapping and an architecture diagram for log flow. Can you share an architecture diagram that shows where redaction occurs (ingest vs. post-processing)?

Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
FintechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: FintechCo logging & PII redaction follow-ups

Alex — thanks, great questions. Answers and attached artifacts below. I tried to keep this concise; happy to run through these on a technical call.

1) Trace IDs and PII: 
- We can preserve trace IDs (X-Trace-ID) while ensuring they are only stored as an opaque hashed token when configured. That means the raw trace value is never persisted in plain text; instead we store a one-way SHA256 token and an internal mapping is never exported. This allows linking events without exposing raw trace values.

2) Header scrubbing: 
- Redwood supports an ingress redaction policy where you can list headers to drop entirely (e.g., Authorization) and headers to mask (e.g., show first 4 chars only). We will provide a policy template tailored to your X-Customer-ID requirement.

3) Cache keys and KV cache: 
- By default, cache keys are normalized and can be configured to use a hashed keying strategy so account identifiers are not present in logs. We also scrub keys before persistence. If you need, we can run a short POC showing cache-safe behavior against a sample workload.

4) Data residency & storage: 
- Logs are stored in the configured region; for Dedicated/Private deploys we can point logs to your VPC S3 bucket. For hosted trials we can store logs in our us-west region with US-only replication disabled.

Attachments included here: redaction_controls_v1.pdf (redaction rules, default regexes, examples), soc2_mapping.xlsx (controls mapping). Also linking an architecture diagram here: https://drive.example.com/fintechco/redaction-controls (see "redaction-flow.png").

Proposed follow-ups:
- Technical deep dive w/ your security engineer + Dylan (30–45m) — Dylan, can you propose times?
- Optional POC: 1-week ingest + redaction validation on a small sample of logs.

If that aligns, I'll have our solutions team draft an MOP and estimate for Dedicated capacity.

Best,

Marissa

Attachments: redaction_controls_v1.pdf, soc2_mapping.xlsx
